messages:
sam: noticed a p99 spike on hosted API v2 starting ~13:20 UTC, p95 up too. queue depth on pool-a climbed to ~240. plots look like a short 15min blip. any obvious noisy tenant? :thinking_face:
elaine: seeing it on the per-route dashboard, latency up ~4x for route /v2/generate. error rate stayed low, only a few 429s.
daphne: kernel-selection logs (kselect) show an increase in generic-fallbacks during the window — fallback_rate jumped from 1.2% -> 16%. maybe kernel mispredictions due to batch sizes changing.
mike: KV cache metrics: hit_ratio dropped from 0.72 -> 0.48, eviction_rate spiked. prefetch queue length climbed as well.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout 2026-03-16T12:04 by @deploy-bot to pool-a (no failures recorded).
sam: running a quick profile: `rt-prof --pool pool-a --since 13:10 --summary`
sam: profiler snippet:
```
time_window: 13:10-13:40
avg_batch_size: 2.1 (normal 7.8)
kernel_fallbacks: 16%
cpu_ms_per_token: +48%
kv_hit_ratio: 0.49
```
jay: that avg_batch_size drop is telling. looks like batching heuristic switched into low-latency mode (batch_target dropped) because we saw many short-sequence requests. small batches -> different kernel chosen -> worse perf for our model.
elaine: tenant logs show a burst of tiny requests from tenant-987 around 13:15-13:25 (short seq len ~8 tokens). concurrency high but requests individually under rate limit.
daphne: kernel selection policy: if batch_size < 4 we prefer 'generic' kernel which is suboptimal for our transformer config. combine that with cold KV cache and you get both increased compute and more memory traffic.
mike: confirmed noisy-tenant pattern: tenant-987 had ~20k requests in 10m, mostly short sequences. caused prefetch thrash and increased eviction churn. silent noisy neighbor because per-request QPS stayed within their quota.
sam: mitigation options: 1) pin pool-a to 'stable-optimized' kernel temporarily 2) bump KV cache allocation on pool-a by +20% and change eviction to lru-ttl hybrid 3) adjust batching policy to maintain batch_target >= 6 for model family-x 4) add alert on kernel_fallback_rate > 5%
elaine: applied kernel pin on pool-a at 13:42 UTC to stable-optimized. monitoring now.
daphne: also pushed a quick batching tweak (min_batch_target=4 -> 6) to the staging runtime config for pool-a at 13:44 (rolling config flag).
mike: KV cache bump queued (requires pool resize), started at 13:45.
sam: early results: p99 dropped back toward baseline by ~13:50, p95 recovering. kernel_fallbacks down to 2.1% by 13:52. KV hit ratio slowly recovering.
jay: root cause summary: short-sequence burst from a single tenant reduced avg batch size which caused our kernel-selection heuristic to pick a fallback kernel that is suboptimal for this model; combined with KV cache eviction thrash from many distinct prefixes -> higher compute/IO per token and queueing.
elaine: follow-ups:
- create a synthetic perf test with mixed tiny+long sequence traffic to validate batching heuristics (owner: eng-runtime, due: EOD next Wed)
- add alert: kernel_fallback_rate > 5% over 5m (owner: eng-sre)
- consider tenant-level burst controls (rate-window vs concurrency) for short-seq heavy tenants (product discussion required)
- KV cache autoscale policy: make short-term bumping faster for pool spikes (infra follow-up)
mike: will open the perf test PR and KV autoscale ticket.
sam: nice work. will keep this thread open until KV hit ratio stabilizes for 24h, but marking triage done for the immediate spike. :thumbsup:
